readme.html:
What's New in v0.5.0

v0.5.0 rebuilds the project workflow around specs. Tickets stay in your tracker, specs live as Markdown in your repo, and each ticket is built with its failing test first, by hand or in an unattended goal run.

Install

  • The plugin now ships from the plugin/ folder on main, listed by the root marketplace entry. The Quick Start commands are unchanged. Updating the plugin installs what main holds, and the separate plugin distribution branch is gone. See plugin/README.md.
  • The workflow commands need uv and a .claude/workflow-config.json, which a setup wizard offers to create. See Tracker Setup.

Adopting an existing codebase

  • intake documents the code, pins its current behavior in characterization tests and records each bug it finds as an F-NNN finding while leaving the behavior unchanged. It also writes a baseline spec and docs/system-description.md, and runs by hand or as one goal with a commit per item. See Intake.

From tickets to a merged spec

  • discovery:create and discovery:approve turn rough input into tickets you approve before they reach the tracker. See Discovery.
  • spec:triage groups tickets into specs. spec:create checks each ticket's readiness against the code, then writes the plan and goal prompt. Specs sit under docs/specs/{todo,completed}/ with a generated INDEX.md. See Specs.
  • ticket:execute and ticket:complete build one ticket test first and commit it with a Ticket: <id> trailer. Neither writes to the tracker. See Tickets.
  • spec:review runs a reviewer panel over the spec diff and a blind verifier per finding, then a rollup and gate. spec:complete opens and merges the PR, closes the tickets, and its docs:verify step checks the README and docs/ for claims the diff made stale, fixing each one only on your yes. spec:status shows where every spec stands. See Review and completion.

Goal runs and the guard

  • spec:create prints launch commands for a goal run over the whole spec or the next batch. The launch denies pushes, PR and issue writes, API writes and questions to you; a stuck ticket is blocked with guard block and the run continues. See Goal Runs.
  • The ticket guard ships inside the plugin as runtime/guard.pyz and runs through uv run. Plugin hooks freeze RED tests, re-run GREEN before a goal run stops and restore ticket context after a compaction. They exit at once unless a ticket is in progress.

Current state and assumptions

  • spec:current checks docs/system-description.md against the code and compiles docs/current-state.json. spec:diff [spec ...] shows what changes if the given specs land in order, with overlaps and each spec's assumptions. See Current state and assumptions.
  • common-ground checks those assumptions against the current state through the assumption-checker agent and keeps its ground file in the repo as docs/COMMON-GROUND.md. See Common Ground.

Agents and trackers

  • Long or parallel work runs in the plugin's agents: code-reader, doc-writer, test-writer, security-prober, architect, reviewer, verifier and assumption-checker. Agents never commit. See Agents.
  • Tracker adapters cover Jira, GitHub Issues, GitHub Projects, Linear and text tickets, plus a GitHub code-host adapter. See Tracker Setup.

Upgrading from 0.4.x

  • The project:<phase>:<command> names are gone. Commands are now discovery:*, spec:* and ticket:*, and "spec" replaces "epic".
  • create-implementation-plan folds into spec:create and complete-epic into spec:complete. complete-sprint and the retrospective phase are removed.
  • common-ground used to keep its file under ~/.claude/common-ground/. When one exists for the repository, it offers to move those assumptions in.

Quick Start

/plugin marketplace add jeffallan/claude-skills

Then, install the skills:

/plugin install fullstack-dev-skills@fullstack-dev-skills

For all installation methods and first steps, see the Quick Start Guide.

Full documentation: jeffallan.github.io/claude-skills

Skills

71 specialized skills across 12 categories covering languages, backend/frontend frameworks, infrastructure, APIs, testing, DevOps, security, data/ML, and platform specialists.

See Skills Guide for the full list, decision trees, and workflow combinations.

Usage Patterns

Context-Aware Activation

Skills activate automatically based on your request:

# Backend Development
"Implement JWT authentication in my NestJS API"
→ Activates: NestJS Expert → Loads: references/authentication.md

# Frontend Development
"Build a React component with Server Components"
→ Activates: React Expert → Loads: references/server-components.md

Multi-Skill Workflows

Complex tasks combine multiple skills:

Feature Development: Feature Forge → Architecture Designer → Fullstack Guardian → Test Master → DevOps Engineer
Bug Investigation:   Debugging Wizard → Framework Expert → Test Master → Code Reviewer
Security Hardening:  Secure Code Guardian → Security Reviewer → Test Master

Context Engineering

Check the assumptions your specs and Claude make against your system's current state with /common-ground. See the Common Ground Guide for full documentation.

Project Workflow

The 13 workflow commands take a group of tickets from your tracker to a reviewed, merged pull request: spec:triage groups tickets into specs, spec:create plans one, ticket:execute and ticket:complete build it test-first (by hand or in an unattended goal run), and spec:review and spec:complete review it and merge it. Specs live as markdown in your repo; tickets stay in Jira, GitHub Issues, GitHub Projects, Linear or text files. See the Workflow Commands Reference. spec:current and spec:diff show the system as it is and what the outstanding specs would change. For an existing codebase, run the intake command first. It documents the code, pins its current behavior in tests and tracks its bugs; see Intake.

flowchart LR
  disc["discovery:create<br>discovery:approve"] -.->|new tickets| triage
  trk["tickets in<br>your tracker"] --> triage["spec:triage"] --> create["spec:create"]
  create --> work["ticket:execute<br>ticket:complete"] --> done["spec:review<br>spec:complete"]
  done -->|merged PR| check["spec:current<br>spec:diff<br>common-ground"]
  check -.->|conflict| create

[!TIP] Setup: the workflow needs uv and a .claude/workflow-config.json, which the first command that needs the tracker offers to create. See Tracker Setup and Goal Runs.
